text:
Hi, I’m Noor Halden, a machine learning engineer with 6 years of experience building and deploying Python-based ML systems. I work across Python, PyTorch, scikit-learn, LangChain, OpenAI API, Hugging Face Transformers, NLP, XGBoost, pandas, and machine learning, and I’m comfortable taking a problem from research and prototyping through testing, deployment, and iteration.

For a recent manufacturing project, I built a camera-based crack and chip detector for Halvorsen Ceramics using Python, PyTorch, YOLOv8, OpenCV, and ONNX. The system was exported to ONNX and run on an industrial PC beside the kiln line. It achieved 97.4% recall on cracks and reduced false rejects from 8% to 2.1%. That work required careful data preparation, model tuning, and practical deployment considerations similar to the kind of production ML engineering you’re looking for.

I also worked on a model deployment pipeline migration for a confidential insurance client, where I moved 9 pricing models from hand-copied pickles to an MLflow registry with automated tests and SageMaker endpoints. That reduced deploy time from 2 days to 35 minutes and eliminated downtime during migration. This experience is directly relevant to your need for version control, testing, deployment, and converting programs into API-based access.

Your role combines Python development, ML experimentation, test data preparation, retraining, statistical analysis, and deployment. I’m comfortable working in that full loop, and I’d approach the work by first understanding the product requirements, then building a reliable proof of concept, validating it with tests and experiments, and iterating based on results. I also value clean code, reproducibility, and practical troubleshooting so the system can be maintained and extended over time.

One note: my background is strongest in Python, OpenCV, ML model development, and deployment pipelines. I haven’t worked directly with GIS, GDAL, Raster, or orthomosaic/orthorectification workflows yet, but I’m confident in learning domain-specific libraries quickly and applying the same engineering discipline I’ve used in other production systems.

What are the first datasets and target outputs you want the proof of concept to focus on?
